titulo: Quiz — Money and the card machine
subtitulo: One lunch bill in Seville: a fifty nobody can break, a machine that wants your currency, and a tip screen watching you
introPt: Quiz time. Lunch is over in a bar in Seville and the whole money chapter arrives at once: the note that's too big, the card machine offering to be helpful in pounds, and the tip screen with its big friendly twenty per cent button. Listen as many times as you like — you're not meant to catch every word, only the moves. Then answer the questions.
cenario: A tourist finishes lunch in a Seville bar and pays: tries cash first, refuses the currency conversion, declines the suggested tip, rounds up with coins and asks for a proper invoice.

dialogo.es: Ahora mismo. Son veintiocho euros con cuarenta.
dialogo.pinyin: ah-OH-rah MEES-moh. sohn bayn-tee-OH-choh EH-oo-rohs kon kwah-REN-tah
dialogo.pt: — Right away. That's twenty-eight euros forty. (the waiter)
— Have you got change for a fifty?

dialogo.es: Uy, de cincuenta no. Lo siento.
dialogo.pinyin: wee, deh theen-KWEN-tah noh. loh SYEN-toh
dialogo.pt: — Oof, not for a fifty. Sorry.
— Fine. Can I pay by card?
— Of course. Here's the card machine.

dialogo.es: ¿Desea pagar en su moneda? En libras le sale más cómodo.
dialogo.pinyin: deh-SEH-ah pah-GAR en soo moh-NEH-dhah. en LEE-brahs leh SAH-leh mahs KOH-moh-dhoh
dialogo.pt: — Would you like to pay in your own currency? In pounds it's easier for you. (here it comes)

dialogo.es: No, gracias. Cóbreme en euros, en moneda local. Sin conversión.
dialogo.pinyin: noh, GRAH-thyahs. KOH-breh-meh en EH-oo-rohs, en moh-NEH-dhah loh-KAL. seen kon-behr-SYON
dialogo.pt: — No thanks. Charge me in euros, in local currency. No conversion.

dialogo.es: Ahora le pide propina: diez, quince o veinte por ciento.
dialogo.pinyin: ah-OH-rah leh PEE-dheh proh-PEE-nah: dyehth, KEEN-theh oh BAYN-teh por THYEN-toh
dialogo.pt: — Now it's asking for a tip: ten, fifteen or twenty per cent.

dialogo.es: Sin propina, gracias. Le dejo el cambio en la mesa.
dialogo.pinyin: seen proh-PEE-nah, GRAH-thyahs. leh DEH-khoh el KAM-byoh en lah MEH-sah
dialogo.pt: — No tip, thanks. I'll leave the coins on the table. (she presses the button and rounds up in cash)

dialogo.es: ¿Me da la factura, por favor? Es para el trabajo.
dialogo.pinyin: meh dah lah fak-TOO-rah, por fah-BOR. es PAH-rah el trah-BAH-khoh
dialogo.pt: — Could I have the invoice, please? It's for work.
— Coming right up. Thanks very much, see you.

perguntas.pergunta: She tries to pay in cash first. Which note is she holding?
perguntas.es: She tries to pay in cash first. Which note is she holding?
perguntas.explica: 'cincuenta' — theen-KWEN-tah. The 'th' at the front is the only thing separating it from 'sesenta' (sixty), and it is on every bar bill in Spain. Listen for the th, not the s.
perguntas.pt: 'cincuenta' — theen-KWEN-tah. The 'th' at the front is the only thing separating it from 'sesenta' (sixty), and it is on every bar bill in Spain. Listen for the th, not the s.

perguntas.pergunta: What does the waiter answer to that?
perguntas.es: What does the waiter answer to that?
opcoes: He can't break it — no change for a fifty
perguntas.explica: 'De cincuenta no. Lo siento.' A small bar genuinely cannot break a fifty early in the day — which is exactly why you ask BEFORE anything is rung up, not while holding the note out.
perguntas.pt: 'De cincuenta no. Lo siento.' A small bar genuinely cannot break a fifty early in the day — which is exactly why you ask BEFORE anything is rung up, not while holding the note out.

perguntas.pergunta: The card machine offers to charge her in pounds, 'because it's easier'. What is that really?
perguntas.es: The card machine offers to charge her in pounds, 'because it's easier'. What is that really?
opcoes: A favour — the rate is the same either way
Currency conversion with a markup that typically runs 10–13%
A legal requirement for foreign cards
perguntas.explica: Dynamic currency conversion. The markup is typically 10–13%, and it must be shown on the screen before you confirm — the pocket rule is that the option displaying YOUR currency is always the wrong one.
perguntas.pt: Dynamic currency conversion. The markup is typically 10–13%, and it must be shown on the screen before you confirm — the pocket rule is that the option displaying YOUR currency is always the wrong one.

perguntas.pergunta: Which phrase does she use to shut the conversion down for good?
perguntas.es: Which phrase does she use to shut the conversion down for good?
opcoes: Cóbreme en euros, en moneda local. Sin conversión.
perguntas.explica: That's the armoured rung of the ladder. Level 1 is 'En euros, por favor' said before the machine reaches you; level 2 is 'Perdone, en euros. Sin conversión.'; and this is level 3, for when they insist. Calm, normal volume, queue or no queue.
perguntas.pt: That's the armoured rung of the ladder. Level 1 is 'En euros, por favor' said before the machine reaches you; level 2 is 'Perdone, en euros. Sin conversión.'; and this is level 3, for when they insist. Calm, normal volume, queue or no queue.

perguntas.pergunta: The screen suggests a 10, 15 or 20 per cent tip. What does she actually do?
perguntas.es: The screen suggests a 10, 15 or 20 per cent tip. What does she actually do?
opcoes: Presses 20 per cent to be safe
Presses 'Sin propina' and leaves the coins on the table
Asks for the service charge to be removed
perguntas.explica: 'Sin propina' — no tip — and then she rounds up in coins. That IS the Spanish system: round up, or leave nothing. Suggested tips on a machine are voluntary, and staff here are on a salary and a collective agreement, so declining harms nobody.

perguntas.pergunta: She asks for 'la factura' rather than 'el tique'. Why does that matter?
perguntas.es: She asks for 'la factura' rather than 'el tique'. Why does that matter?
opcoes: It's the polite word for a receipt
It's the invoice with her details — the one an employer or insurer accepts
It's the itemised bill before paying
perguntas.explica: 'Un tique' is the little till slip; 'la factura' carries your name and details, and it's the document an expenses system or an insurer will accept. Ask at the counter, while the transaction is still on their screen.
